Returns completionSource.TrySetCanceled(); queued asynchronously by the cancellation callback.
Logs cancellation and queues TryCancelCompletion with Task.Run using a cached Func<bool>; does not wait for that task.
Evaluates expected matcher first. On match attempts result completion; otherwise asks the optional unexpected-message selector for an exception or logs an ignored message.
Adds a stack-message callback to the listener list; it is invoked on each quick report.
Existing WaitFor name preserved. Creates completion and callback context, adds message processing, and registers cancellation. Registration ownership differs by version and is not changed.
Existing WaitFor name preserved; delegates to the three-argument overload with a null unexpected-message selector.
Snapshots callbacks with ToList before invoking each with the reported message; callback exceptions are not swallowed here.
Stores the observed layer and subscribes DispatchQuickReport to its quick-report event.
Returns the construction-time UTC timestamp used to discard read errors from an older communication session.
Closes the HID device under the connection lock, clears cached features, optionally notifies connection state, cancels and awaits the receive task, and schedules reconnect when broken and enabled.

Reads while the HID device is open/readable, validates reports, assembles sequential fragments, and enqueues an inbound USB message on the end flag. Sequence failure suppresses delivery; cancellation exits quietly; read failure queues UsbReadFailedMessage. It does not add a received-byte-count check.

Opens the HID device, honors discovery timing, queries SupportedEmiType with one retry, restores a still-supported active EMI type, records the open time, and starts the receive task. Failure closes communication before rethrowing.

Guards against overlapping restart, stops the reconnect timer, closes as broken, delays 100 ms and starts communication again. Rearms reconnect on error and clears the guard in finally. Only 6.4 additionally invokes Reconnected subscribers after startup.
Returns false when already restarting or when RestartCommunicationAsync throws; returns true after it succeeds.
Awaits the state-machine trigger, then updates/notifies InterfaceConnectionState from CLOSED/OPEN/BROKEN. OPEN preserves an existing MediumFailure state.
Attempts TryRestartCommunicationAsync with events; fires Reconnected on success, otherwise rearms the reconnect timer when enabled.

State-machine write action: reconnects a broken interface unless restart is already in progress, validates payload length 1..907, writes generated HID fragments in order, and completes the send. Failure faults the send, schedules reconnect when enabled and returns BROKEN.
CompletedTask no-op callback used by transition-table entries that keep the current state; it performs no write or close.
Broken-trigger callback starts the reconnect timer only for a nonnegative reconnect interval, then returns CompletedTask.
CompletedTask no-op callback used on opened/closed/reconnected state changes; the state-machine executor performs the state update.
State-machine getter callback reads the target interface state without changing it.
State-machine setter callback assigns the requested state; connection notifications are handled by FireEventAsync.
Invokes PropertyChanged with this instance and a new PropertyChangedEventArgs.
Enqueues the USB stack message, then waits on its send-completion source with a 1000 ms timeout.
Writes RawBytes through the HID device only while open; timeout and write errors update statistics, receive diagnostic context, and are rethrown.
Creates a DeviceFeatureGet message and installs its matching LayerListener before sending, then waits for the response with timeout and diagnostic error handling.
Builds DeviceFeatureSet HID body and queues an outbound FeatureService message with send completion.
Checks report ID 1, at most 61 data bytes, fragmentation/sequence constraints and full nonfinal fragments; sequence zero is accepted only for a single start/end report.
Rejects a mismatching EMI type unless none is known, then learns it and dispatches the telegram message.
Accepts BusConnectionState response/info reports, interprets byte 1 as Connected and other values as MediumFailure, and notifies only on change.
Invokes MessageReceived subscribers and logs subscriber exceptions without rethrowing.
Pads/truncates to 64 bytes and writes to writable primary/secondary streams; rewinds the secondary stream if seekable. A missing primary stream throws IOException.
Reads one 64-byte report from the primary stream. Short reads return null; IOException closes and rethrows; cancellation returns null only when the primary stream has already been cleared.
Unix reader polls the descriptor in 1000 ms intervals and returns only a 64-byte read. IOException closes the device and returns null; other errors are logged and return null.
Task.Run callback invokes WriteReport with the captured device and data.
Task.Run delegate forwards to the Unix polling reader.
Returns false for a zero handle; otherwise converts it to an integer descriptor and checks libc close returns zero.
Enumerates an interface index and attempts detail/path retrieval; returns true even when detail retrieval fails and devicePath remains null.
Rejects nonmatching HID paths; probes read/write access with a shared handle, then creates a device even if both capabilities remain false.

Reads hid-generic uevent identity or resolves the sysfs parent to idVendor/idProduct, probes /dev read/write access and creates a Unix HID device. Requested ID filters apply only in the uevent branch; the fallback does not apply them.
Exact Path equality predicate used by FirstOrDefault during USB interface discovery.
Accepts only FeatureService USB messages carrying DeviceFeatureResponse for the requested feature; returns its value tuple, otherwise false/null.
Exact libc realpath entry point; managed alias and argument roles follow the import and inspected HID caller. Native binding/flags/marshaling stay unchanged.
Exact libc open entry point; managed alias and argument roles follow the import and inspected HID caller. Native binding/flags/marshaling stay unchanged.

Compares the translation language key with the captured culture name; this predicate is passed to FirstOrDefault for the requested culture.
Compares the translation language key with the captured culture name; this predicate is passed to FirstOrDefault for the immediate parent culture.

Returns the first exact-culture translation, then the first immediate-parent translation, then default text. Null translation values trigger fallback; empty values do not.
Reads the unsigned Version attribute from the document root, returning zero when it is absent. Invalid attribute text can throw.
OrderByDescending callback extracts the document version from a source/document pair. Preserve the previously restored 6.3 constructor-lambda name.
Dictionary key selector returns the parsed USB vendor/product identifier pair. Preserve the previously restored 6.3 constructor-lambda name.

Parses hexadecimal USB/KNX identifiers, localized text, volatile-address/USB-fix flags, medium and optional timings. Missing persistence defaults true; missing medium uses RF in default text, otherwise TP1. Preserve the restored 6.3 constructor-lambda name.

Loads candidates in descending version order, retaining the first catalog that parses into the identifier dictionary. Per-catalog construction errors are logged and tried again; document enumeration/version-sort errors are not caught here.
Assigns the parsed interface definition used to enrich USB discovery results.
Replaces the lazy default catalog only when the supplied document version is strictly higher; records update as the load source.
Iterator loads knx_interfaces.xml from existing candidate paths and then the embedded resource. It yields source/document pairs and disposes enumeration/stream resources; parse/I/O errors propagate.

Reads the saved ia attribute for this HID path and converts it to IndividualAddress. Missing files/settings or caught XML/read errors return null; preserve the existing readable method name.
Loads or creates devices XML, inserts/updates a setting keyed by HID path, stores the individual address and saves. XML/save failures are logged; directory creation occurs outside that catch.
Returns 1700 ms when DeviceDescriptor bit 0x20 is set, otherwise 80 ms (also when features are absent); callers use it as the delay between writing and verifying local memory.
Returns 1000 ms when DeviceDescriptor masked by 0xFFF0 equals 0x1010, otherwise 500 ms, including absent features.
Writes 1 at EMI1 local memory 265, then the Busmonitor/other mode byte 144/18 at 96; verifies both writes. Existing 6.4 async carrier names corroborate the operation.
Resets the local interface through Emi1ResetAsync when EMI1 is active, otherwise MResetAsync, with a 3500 ms wait and CancellationToken.None. The local management instance is disposed.
Reads one byte from EMI1 local memory 265, 278 and 96 into nullable saved fields for later restoration. This captures settings in memory, not on disk.
Writes and verifies each captured non-null setting at 278, 265 and 96, in that order. A failed write propagates; saved fields are not cleared.
Optionally captures BCU settings, initializes PEI type and communication mode, then writes zero to EMI1 local memory 278. The original 6.4 async carrier confirms the initializer name.

Persists the individual address for volatile configurations, restores BCU settings when the interface is open in EMI1 mode, and resets an open EMI1 interface in finally even if persistence/restoration fails. It does not close the HID transport.
Requires a PC value response and delegates request-specific matching to IsConfirmation. A zero-length confirmation matches here, then becomes a read failure in the caller.

Sends PC_GetValue_req, awaits a matching confirmation, returns nonempty memory data, and retries once after a 200 ms delay on timeout with a 200 ms larger response timeout. Cancellation propagates. Registration is removed around response wait/retry; the initial send is outside that finally, so send failures do not run that removal.
Extracts one UInt32 at four times the index from the optional PID_RF_MULTI_LL_TIMEOUT_VALUES response. Caller enumerates exactly five indices only when response data is present.

Reads individual/domain addresses and PL/RF configuration using cEMI properties or EMI1 memory. RF multi acknowledgement records are read in chunks of at most 15; five link-layer timeouts and filtering mode are optional. Saves the reception band on the connector and returns a BusInterfaceConfiguration. Errors propagate and the local interface is disposed.
Combines cEMI address properties 0/57 and 0/58, or reads two EMI1 bytes at address 279, then returns IndividualAddress. Uses the caller cancellation token.
Reads cEMI property 0/82 only as a six-byte domain, or EMI1 memory 258 only as a two-byte domain. Null/wrong-length buffers return DomainAddress.None; read errors propagate.
Tries cEMI property 0/11 and returns its serial number when data exists, otherwise SerialNumber.None. The supplied cancellation token is unused; the request uses CancellationToken.None.

Uses EMI1 memory 78, an active local transport service, or PID_DEVICE_DESCRIPTOR as appropriate. Local-mode LocalServiceNotSupported returns UInt16.MaxValue; other local read errors propagate. The general property fallback infers PL before RF before TP from medium bits. All requests use CancellationToken.None.
Matches the master-data descriptor Version against the captured numeric device descriptor, enabling a medium-type override when direct medium data is unavailable.
Compares the cache entry path with the captured HID device path using exact string equality; caller uses FirstOrDefault to retrieve features.
Uses the same exact path comparison before inserting newly read features. Caller keeps at most four entries and does not refresh order on a cache hit.

Reads device descriptor, serial number, APDU size, medium, communication modes, busmonitor time base, programming-mode support and RF/filtering capabilities. Initial feature-service descriptor failures are swallowed; later cEMI descriptor fallback may propagate errors. Missing medium uses descriptor/master-data fallback or TP1; explicit medium flags prefer PL over RF. RF physical-feature read failure uses ScanFx|TxFx|FastAck. Several property reads intentionally use CancellationToken.None. In the non-cEMI path, the BCU programming-mode test runs only when a descriptor fallback was needed.
Returns GroupAddress for the stable OrderBy before duplicate detection.
Returns GroupAddress for grouping to detect duplicate acknowledgement addresses.
Returns Count(group) > 1 for the duplicate-address warning.
Returns the duplicate group Key for the warning message.
Returns GroupAddress to regroup sorted acknowledgements before selecting one per address.
Returns Enumerable.First(group), preserving the first sorted acknowledgement for a duplicate address.
Writes the configured individual address bytes to EMI1 local memory 279 using the supplied cancellation token.
Writes individual-address high and low bytes to properties 0/57 then 0/58. Uses the supplied token; these are writes without readback verification.

Writes a two-byte domain to EMI1 memory 258 when required, then reads/modifies memory 257. Enabling the PL repeater clears bit 16; disabling sets it. differencesOnly compares the stored configuration.
Writes a two-byte domain to property 0/70 when required, then reads/modifies property 0/73. Enabling the PL repeater clears bit 4; disabling sets it. Uses the supplied token.

Sorts by group address, warns about duplicate groups and keeps the first acknowledgement per address. Writes the two-byte count at property 8/1/70 index zero with CancellationToken.None, then up to 15 three-byte records per request with the supplied token. Property-write exceptions are logged and rethrown; sorting/grouping failures occur before that catch.

Encodes at most five UInt32 timeouts. Zero entries use the current configuration array, or the default array if it is null. Writes property 19/1/96 with CancellationToken.None; the supplied token is unused. Write failures are warned and swallowed, but preparation/indexing errors precede that catch.

Maps Busmonitor to 1, Raw to 2 and supported LocalTransportLayer to 6. Other cases select 224 only when RF Multi retry option 2 is supported and the effective RF Multi setting is enabled; an unspecified connector setting counts as enabled. Otherwise returns 0.

Uses configuration or connector RF Multi preference. Writes property 19/51 when known, otherwise reads it. Failures are logged and swallowed without clearing a requested true value. If true, writes additional-info selection 8/72 as zero in busmonitor and one otherwise. All reads/writes use CancellationToken.None. The success log always says one even when zero was written.
Reads optional time-base property 8/55 with CancellationToken.None. A present response updates the UInt16 time-base field; absent data logs unsupported and leaves the prior field intact.

Selects and write-verifies property 8/52 with zero delay and CancellationToken.None. On ModeNotSupported it best-effort reads supported modes. 6.4 throws an enriched UsbConnectorException, including in busmonitor mode; it has no 6.3 retry branch. After success, RF descriptor 8977 in LinkLayer mode best-effort writes filtering property 8/66, swallowing its failures.

Falls back from known-unsupported busmonitor to LinkLayer before setup, creates a timeout-configured local management scope, sets communication mode, reads time base for busmonitor, and configures RF Multi mode/timeouts for supported RF interfaces. Unsupported explicitly requested RF Multi is logged. The management scope is disposed.
Dispatches active EMI1 to InitializeLocalDeviceEmi1Async with the save flag; every other EMI type uses InitializeLocalDeviceCEmiAsync.

Writes a six-byte RF domain when required. On RF Multi changes sets communication/RF mode, then changed acknowledgement and timeout arrays. Reception mode and slow-mode destination-check writes are best-effort, including swallowed cancellation. Filtering changes are written outside those catches and can fail the operation. differencesOnly compares stored configuration.
Snapshots the PropertyChanged delegate and invokes it with this connector and the supplied property name when non-null.
Scans cEMI additional-info headers from offset two and returns the first requested ID offset, or -1. Advances by each stored payload length plus two.

Logs the received message and, when supported and present, its RF Multi/ack info. Invokes the receive delegate with the parsed message and memory over the original raw byte array; does not copy the payload.

Adds/replaces RF Multi transmission/reception settings using the connector RF band. A non-Ready transmission to an individual destination expects one fast ack and adds short-ack slot zero; other cases expect zero. An absent reception mode uses Current.

If a reset timestamp is pending, waits the elapsed milliseconds when elapsed is below one second (not the remaining interval), clears the timestamp, then unless initialization is suppressed reselects cEMI and writes/verifies PID_COMM_MODE 8/52. Uses CancellationToken.None. This records the existing delay behavior without correcting it.

Atomically reads pending routing-busy count. If nonzero, adds randomized 0..count*50ms jitter to the last advertised busy wait and subtracts the observed count; otherwise returns the default 20ms spacing. Concurrent newer notifications remain pending.
Records a routing-busy notification by incrementing its pending count and replacing the advertised wait duration in milliseconds. The incoming routing-busy handler supplies that duration.
Computes the next spacing, delays only its remainder since the previous release time and records the current time after the wait. Does not accept cancellation or serialize concurrent callers itself.

For a bus message, replaces its source with the connector individual address, clears repeated status, changes L_Data_req to L_Data_ind at its caller, and clears system-broadcast status unless enabled and allowed by the send filter. Other message types are unchanged.
Uses the bus message directly or reparses its raw data, then tests its system-broadcast flag. Parse failures retain their original propagation behavior.

Sends system broadcasts as RoutingSystemBroadcastFrame using the dedicated multicast communication when available. Other messages become RoutingIndicationFrame and pass through the existing optional secure wrapper before the normal multicast send.
Builds a 16-byte block from a big-endian 48-bit sequence, 48-bit serial number, 16-bit message tag and 16-bit payload length. High sequence bits are discarded.
Builds the sequence/serial/tag counter block with byte 14 set to 0xFF and byte 15 initially zero.

Clones the initial counter block, encrypts successive blocks with AES-128 ECB and increments only byte 15. Requests over 4096 bytes are rejected. Retains the original stream/padding and disposal behavior.

XORs the encrypted MAC with the start of the counter key stream and the encrypted payload with bytes after the reserved MAC block. Returns payload and outputs the plain MAC separately; this helper does not authenticate either result.
Calculates the plain IP CCM MAC over the frame header with no payload, then encrypts that MAC using the notification timestamp, serial and message tag.
Returns the event timestamp.

Returns the acceptance decision set by the transition action.

Converts the timing abstraction UTC time to unsigned Unix milliseconds.
Chooses an inclusive random delay between the bounds; when maximum is no greater than minimum returns maximum. Retains the int range conversion.
Promotes zero delay to one, stops the timer, divides the interval by the timing speed factor, records update/periodic purpose and restarts the one-shot timer.

Clears the update-scheduled flag and invokes the send callback. Replies reuse the captured request serial/tag; ordinary notifications generate a new random tag and use the local serial. Callback exceptions fault the task.

Only writes the existing A0 diagnostic; leaves timer/context unchanged.

Arms a non-update notification using the configured initial-delay range.
Sets the time-keeper role flag.

Updates/checks synchronization, becomes a follower, then schedules a periodic notification.

Starts the pending update reply, becomes time keeper and schedules a periodic notification without awaiting the send.
Returns the current 16-bit tag and increments it with wraparound; does not add synchronization.

With a routing key, records secure-send statistics, allocates a message tag, captures group time, constructs an authenticated wrapper and notifies the timer of that send. Otherwise records a plain send and returns the original frame.
When a routing key exists, records notification statistics and forwards timestamp/serial/tag to the group timer. The caller has already checked authenticity.

Returns messages carried by routing indication/system-broadcast frames. Busy frames update send pacing under the connector lock; lost/unknown frames update diagnostics and return null. Unknown frames invoke the unhandled-frame delegate.

Applies system-broadcast policy, enforces configured secure/plain frame mode, validates wrapper/notification authentication and group-timer acceptance, then dispatches the inner/plain payload. Records each rejection and retains existing unhandled-frame callback behavior.

Processes a frame, suppresses one echo matching the pending confirmation by source/destination/length/APCI, then emits raw data and bus-message events outside Info mode. The comparison does not compare payload bytes.

FilterOff accepts immediately. IP-router filtering requires APCI and accepts network-parameter read/response with object type 0, PID 11 and first test byte 1; serial-number domain writes with a four-byte domain; or system-broadcast secure sync/data-with-confidentiality services. Other inputs are invalid. Retains the unchecked first test-byte access.

Requires a routing system-broadcast frame containing a flagged bus message; otherwise returns NonSystemBroadcast. Disabled system broadcasts are Invalid, and enabled messages pass through the configured receive filter.

Returns Undefined if fewer than six bytes, header length below six or protocol version other than 0x10; otherwise reads the big-endian service code at offset two. Does not validate total frame length.
Invokes the frame delegate when present and catches/logs subscriber exceptions.
Tests whether the unicast address equals the configured local address.
Requires IPv4 support and any unicast address matching the captured local address; caches the address predicate.

Forwards only routing system-broadcast frames to the dedicated receiver.
Copies the configured KNX address into the connector field.

Parses the received bytes with the transport LocalEndPoint and no decryption key, logs/diagnoses the inbound frame, then invokes Received. Does not catch parse or subscriber failures.

Catches most transport errors, records selected exceptions and raises Closed unless disposing; socket-backed IO errors attempt disposal and raise Closed unconditionally. Exceptions from handlers/diagnostics may still fault the task. Existing misleading ReceiveAsync log text is unchanged.

Receives into a 4096-byte buffer with no cancellation token while the socket is open. On EndOfMessage, delivers only the current receive Count bytes; earlier fragments are not accumulated. Handles cancellation/transport errors and may dispose before Closed; the disposal path awaits the retained receive task, so its potential self-await is preserved for final behavior verification.
